$comment: GBS EMISSION POLICY — the single machine-readable source for the banned-attr rule (unified remediation plan, Phase 3 / F1). Laravel's StrictAttrValidator reads this file; the brain keeps a committed copy at workers/brain/src/domain/contract/spectra-contract.json whose byte-equality is asserted by vitest (drift = red CI). The rendering GRAMMAR (variants, arbitrary-value rules, palette) ships via the spectra-blocks plugin metadata export ('contract' key, grammar v2+) — derived there from the constants the JIT compiler itself consumes, so it cannot drift from rendering behavior. Ownership split is deliberate and exclusive: the plugin may not declare emission policy (it briefly did, grammar v1 'banned_attrs' — removed 2026-06-12: hand-typed, unconsumed plugin-side, and spoke for third-party namespaces); this file declares no rendering grammar except `state_tail`, the class state-key tail grammar the converter mints keys within and the plugin renders keys within, and `fa_cell`, the attribute the converter marks a Font Awesome `<i>` with and the plugin draws Font Awesome 7's cell on: the converter mints both offline, before any site is reachable, so the published grammar has to be the shared one.

transitional.$comment: style.spacing.* subtree tolerated until the delegated GBS-only migration removes the last structural-spacing emitter (CounterTransform). Delete together with StrictAttrValidator::TRANSITIONAL_STYLE_SPACING_TOLERANCE and its pinning test.

notes.update_ops: apply_change updateBlockAttributes is clientId-targeted (no block name at validation time) — the 13-key ban applies name-agnostically there until a name plumb lands (plan Phase 3D leftover). Insert/replace BlockSpecs carry `name` and are scope-aware.

state_tail.$comment: The class STATE-TAIL grammar: the selector text a GBS class state key may carry after its class (`.nav-link` + `[href^="/"]`). spectra-blocks StateResolver renders a verbatim state key only when it is a tail of this grammar (anything else renders nothing); block-converter mints class-state keys only within it and writes a rule whose tail it refuses to wrapperStyles, so no rule is dropped. The character classes are mirrored by block-converter src/payload/stateTail.ts STATE_TAIL and spectra-blocks StateResolver::TAIL, each pinned to this block by a test (spectra-blocks keeps a byte copy of this file at tests/phpunit/tests/GlobalStyles/fixtures/spectra-contract.json). `vectors` is GENERATED from the grammar (block-converter tests/support/stateTailVectors.ts --write) and both scanners are tested on it. `excluded` is refused everywhere, quoted or not: `<` can close the <style> element, braces the rule, a line break a string. `excluded_unquoted` is refused outside a quoted string: `/` is the only way to spell a CSS comment delimiter. A `(` opens only the arguments of a pseudo the scanner read, never after `url_ident` (ASCII case-insensitive): an ident spelled `url` followed by `(` is a CSS url-token, in which a quote opens no string and the token runs to the first `)`. The one property all of this keeps: every string, comment, bracket and url-token a tail could open closes inside it, so the rule after it stays intact (block-converter tests/stateTail.test.ts checks it with a CSS tokenizer). `version` names the grammar, and each version accepts every tail the one before it accepts: a renderer at the converter's version or later renders every key the converter mints, so wp-importer ensureStateTailGrammar passes a plugin whose advertised version is at least the converter's and reads no other field. Any change to the grammar, its character classes or its vectors takes a new version (block-converter tests/stateTail.test.ts pins a digest of them to each version).
grammar: pseudo  = ':' [ ':' ] name [ '(' args ')' ]        (name: pseudo_ident+; before '(' never url_ident, ASCII case-insensitive)
args    = { string | escape | pseudo | '[' attr ']' | char }
string  = q { escape | any - q - escape - excluded } q        (q: one of quotes)
char    = any - excluded - excluded_unquoted - quotes - escape - '(' - ')' - '[' - ']'

fa_cell.$comment: The Font Awesome CELL mark: the attribute block-converter writes on every Font Awesome `<i>` of a page that carries a `<link data-type="preview-runtime">` — the icon stylesheet the page assembler gives the PREVIEW (Font Awesome 7, unlayered over a layered page), which the converter strips and WordPress never loads. spectra-blocks FontAwesomeIcons draws Font Awesome 7's element and size rules on a marked `<i>` only; an unmarked `<i>` is an import's, whose own Font Awesome sheet (any version) rides the page's imports, and gets the glyph alone. Mirrored by block-converter src/normalize/strip.ts FA_CELL_ATTR and spectra-blocks FontAwesomeIcons::CELL_ATTR, each pinned to this block by a test.
